`bun nv owners --closes goal-closeout` names the rest of the gaps, across many crates. Take them one directory at a time, smallest first. Stage 4 stops on `BLOCKED` only for "too large", which the goal's § *Stage 4* defines. `bun nv import` is broken, because the rule index it reads was deleted. Goal `ci-green`'s floor check stays red until Stage 6. That is expected.

items.text: **A path of many missing folders is slow to refuse** — gap `a-path-of-many-missing-folders-is-slow-to-refuse`, at `crates/nvs-config/src/capability.rs:932` (`resolved`). The record calls a length bound a decision. A fix without a new refusal: the walk only ever tries ancestors inside the trailing run of `Normal` components (it returns `None` at the first `..`, root or prefix), so binary-search the deepest prefix in that run that `Files::canonical` answers, for O(log n) calls. It gives the walk's answer exactly when "a prefix resolves" is monotone along plain names. Write that argument in the doc comment, and check the case where a folder the OS can traverse still fails to canonicalize (an ACL that denies reading it). Run the `nvs-runtime` capability tests, whose `Files` doubles may not be prefix-closed. The hostile case `tests/hostile/tools/install/when-something-is-refused/02-a-path-two-million-folders-deep.nvs` carries the gap's `// proof:` marker, and that line goes when the record goes.
